record.original_question: Let M be the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on R^d, defined by M f(x) = sup_{r>0} (1/m(B(x,r))) ∫_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, where B(x,r) is the open ball of center x and radius r, and let the uncentered maximal operator be defined analogously by taking the supremum over all open balls that contain x. Is the map f -> |∇M f| bounded from the Sobolev space W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^1(R^d)? Equivalently, for every f in W^{1,1}(R^d), is M f weakly differentiable and does there exist a universal constant C = C(d) such that ||∇M f||_{L^1(R^d)} <= C ||∇f||_{L^1(R^d)}? The same question is asked for the uncentered maximal operator.

evidence.quote: For f ∈ L1loc (Rd ) we define the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function M f by M f (x) = sup_{r>0} 1/m(B(x, r)) ∫_{B(x,r)} |f (y)| dy, where B(x, r) is the open ball of center x and radius r, and m(B(x, r)) denotes its d-dimensional Lebesgue measure. The uncentered maximal function is defined analogously, taking the supremum of averages over open balls that contain the point x, but that are not necessarily centered at x.

Question 1 (Hajlasz and Onninen, 2004 - cf. [16]). Is the operator f 7→ |∇M f| bounded from W 1,1 (Rd) to L1 (Rd)? Same question for the uncentered operator. Naturally, this involves proving that M f is weakly differentiable, and establishing the bound ||∇M f||_{L1(Rd)} ≤ C (||f||_{L1(Rd)} + ||∇f||_{L1(Rd)}).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and, for $f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, define the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function
$$Mf(x)=\sup_{r>0}\frac{1}{m(B(x,r))}\int_{B(x,r)}|f(y)|\,dy,$$
where $B(x,r)$ is the open Euclidean ball of center $x$ and radius $r$ and $m$ denotes $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Define the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function $\widetilde{M}f(x)$ analogously, taking the supremum of averages $\frac{1}{m(B)}\int_B|f(y)|\,dy$ over all open balls $B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ that contain $x$. Let $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the Sobolev space of integrable functions whose distributional gradient lies in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$.

Prove or disprove: for every $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the function $Mf$ is weakly differentiable, and there exists a constant $C=C(d)$, independent of $f$, such that
$$\|\nabla Mf\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}\le C\,\|\nabla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}.$$
Equivalently, decide whether the sublinear map $f\mapsto |\nabla Mf|$ is bounded from $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$. The same question is posed with $M$ replaced by the uncentered maximal operator $\widetilde{M}$.
artifact.category_tag: Endpoint Sobolev regularity of maximal operators
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is known in dimension one: Tanaka (and Aldaz–Pérez Lázaro with sharp constant 1) settled the uncentered case, and Kurka established the centered case in $d=1$. Partial results are known in higher dimensions for special classes (e.g., radial functions, block-decreasing functions, Hardy–Sobolev variants), but the full endpoint $W^{1,1}\to L^1$ gradient bound for both the centered and uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge 2$, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of Maximal Operators: Recent Progress and Some Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Question 1 (Hajlasz and Onninen, 2004) ... Same question for the uncentered operator.
status_evidence.claim: The Hajłasz–Onninen endpoint $W^{1,1}$ question is recorded as an open problem, with the one-dimensional case resolved by Tanaka and Kurka.

status_evidence.title: The one-dimensional centred maximal function diminishes the variation
status_evidence.snippet: Kurka proved that the centred Hardy-Littlewood maximal function is bounded on BV(R).

status_evidence.title: Maximal Function Methods for Sobolev Spaces (AMS Surveys 257)
status_evidence.snippet: endpoint regularity in higher dimensions remains open
status_evidence.claim: The higher-dimensional endpoint Sobolev regularity problem for the Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator remains open.
